what_it_does: Modern camera sensors capture millions of pixels per frame, producing far more raw data than is actually needed for a downstream AI vision task (like detecting objects). Transmitting and storing all those pixels wastes energy. This paper proposes building a tiny, task-aware compression stage directly inside the image sensor itself — before the data ever leaves the chip. A compact 1-bit encoder (one that reduces each value to a single binary digit, the most aggressive form of compression) is trained jointly with the downstream vision task so it learns to preserve only the information that actually matters for that task. Because the encoder lives on the sensor chip, the data shrinks at the source, dramatically cutting transmission bandwidth and energy. The approach is described as "compressive learning" — computing a compact learned representation at capture time rather than sending raw pixels.
